ideas.description: Exploit: add progressive resizing to the E018 incumbent (2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655, CUDA-graphed step, 9.5 epochs, 0.7571 @ 8.16 s). This is E015's contingency moved onto the faster, higher-margin base. Train 11 epochs in total. Epochs 1-5 use whole augmented images downscaled to 24 px on the GPU (bilinear F.interpolate, AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) head pooling as in E011/E015). Epochs 6-11 run at 32 px. Define the LR schedule (triangular plus Lookahead, as in the incumbent) over total steps. Batch 1536 with drop_last at both resolutions. Capture one CUDA graph per resolution in build and warm both on synthetic data, so nothing recompiles or recaptures in the timed region. Everything else stays at E018. Log per-phase ms/step.
ideas.expected: Time about 7.5-7.7 s (-6 to -8%). That assumes about 0.85 s per full-res epoch and about 0.49 s per 24 px epoch: 5x0.49 + 6x0.85 + 0.06 prepare. Accuracy 0.754-0.758, centred near 0.756: E015's -0.43 pp from resizing, plus about +0.45 pp for the extra half full-res epoch, on top of 0.7571. If it reaches >=0.755, it becomes the incumbent; next, trim 0.5 full-res epochs. If it reaches 0.751-0.753, move to 5 low-res + 6.5 full-res epochs.

ideas.description: Exploit the margin and measure the epoch slope on the current recipe. On E018, change only the epoch count, from 9.5 to 9.25 (32 steps/epoch at batch 1536 with drop_last, so 296 steps instead of 304), with the LR schedule stretched to match. Nothing else changes. The result gives the pp-per-second exchange rate on the graphed batch-1536 net, the reference for scoring every later per-step cut.
ideas.expected: Time about 7.93-7.98 s (-2.5%, about -0.21 s). Accuracy 0.7535-0.7560, centred near 0.7549, from about 0.9 pp/epoch. If it holds >=0.7545, it becomes the incumbent and the slope is <=1 pp/epoch. If it falls below 0.753, the slope at this point is steeper (>1.6 pp/epoch), so stop trimming epochs and spend the margin only on per-step cuts.

ideas.description: On E018, set an LR floor: the decay phase ends at 5% of the peak LR instead of 0, for both the Muon group and the SGD groups (bias, BN, head). Shape: linear from the peak to 0.05x peak over the existing decay steps. Warmup, Lookahead, epochs and batch are unchanged. The LR tensor in the CUDA graph is just a different precomputed schedule, so nothing needs recapturing.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.2 pp, about 0.757-0.759. If it gains >=0.15 pp, keep it and trade the gain for about -0.15 epoch. If it loses >=0.1 pp, the decay-to-zero tail is doing useful annealing in this short schedule; close H1.7.5.

ideas.description: Explore whether smaller Muon batches keep buying accuracy now that per-step overhead is graphed away. E017 showed 2000 -> 1536 gave +0.16 pp at unchanged per-image cost. On E018, switch to batch 1024: Muon lr 0.205*sqrt(1024/1536) = 0.167 and momentum 0.70, with the SGD-group lr scaled linearly with batch. Keep 9.5 epochs (48 steps/epoch, 456 steps). Recapture the CUDA graph at the new batch shape in build.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.05 to +0.25 pp, about 0.7575-0.7595. Time +1 to +4% (about 8.25-8.45 s), since conv efficiency may start to drop at 1024. It wins only if the gain is >=0.2 pp per +1% time; then trade it for about -0.25 epoch. If accuracy is flat or lower, 1536 is the batch optimum; close the batch axis.

ideas.description: Explore the next group-1 cut, extending E009's depth cut. On E018, reduce group 1 from 2 convs to 1, keeping only the 32x32 whitening-output -> 128 conv followed by pool/BN/GELU, and removing the remaining 16x16 128->128 conv. Raise epochs from 9.5 to 10.25 to compensate. Also record a one-step torch.profiler breakdown (conv vs BN/activation/pool kernels per stage) in the smoke test, which tests H2.4.1.
ideas.expected: Per-step time -8 to -10% (one 16x16 conv, matching E009's 9%), so train time at 10.25 epochs is about 7.9-8.1 s (-1 to -3%). Accuracy 0.752-0.757: the cut probably costs more than E009's 0.29 pp because group 1 then has no 16x16 conv, recovered by about +0.7 pp from the extra epochs. It wins only if it is >=0.754 at <8.0 s. The profiler should show >=40% of GPU time in non-conv kernels at 32x32/16x16. If not, H2.4's memory-bandwidth mechanism is weakened.

ideas.description: Noise calibration on the incumbent, with no recipe change. Add an internal salt to the data-order/augmentation generator (the trial seeds stay 0, 1, 2) and run E018 with salt=1. The pre-registered comparison is against E018's 0.7571 (salt 0); a second salt run is optional. Per-seed accuracies are logged.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±1%). 3-seed mean within 0.7555-0.7590, and |delta| vs 0.7571 of 0.1-0.3 pp. A |delta| >=0.2 pp means every pending verdict with an effect <0.2 pp (E017, H1.7.5, epoch trims) must be treated as inconclusive, and a >=0.755 margin is required before keeping a time cut.

structured_output.summary: The incumbent is E018: 2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536, CUDA-graphed step, 9.5 epochs, 0.7571 @ 8.16 s, with about 0.41 pp of margin to spend. The top exploit stacks progressive resizing (5 epochs at 24 px + 6 at 32 px, 11 in total) on this faster, higher-margin base. E015 showed resizing costs about 0.5 pp/s, half the epoch line, so I expect about 0.756 at 7.6 s. The second exploit trims to 9.25 epochs (about 7.95 s, about 0.755). That banks the margin and also measures the epoch exchange rate on the current recipe. Two lower-priority explores tune Muon: an LR floor at 5% of peak (H1.7.5), and batch 1024 with sqrt-scaled lr (extending E017's batch finding). Two more are information-oriented: a group-1 cut to 1 conv with +0.75 epoch, plus a profiler breakdown (H2.4/H2.4.1), and a salted replicate to calibrate perturbation noise (H4.1.1), which many small-delta verdicts depend on. I021 (EMA, H4.2.1) stays queued, which brings the queue to 7. I left H1.2.1 (flip) and H1.3.2 (Cutout) without ideas, because both can only confirm what the incumbent already does and neither would improve time.
